question.text: What is the MAXIMUM investment a standard (non-LVF) Category III AIF can make in one investee company, directly or through units of other AIFs?

answer.text: 10% of investable funds (or NAV, as elected and disclosed in PPM)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Standard Cat III AIFs face a 10% concentration limit on investable funds (or NAV, if elected and disclosed in PPM). LVFs get 20%. **The Trap:** 5%/15% are not prescribed thresholds. 20% applies only to LVFs. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cat I/II (XIX-A) use 25% concentration — Cat III is tighter because of leverage. **Distributor's Pro-Tip:** Confirm in the PPM whether concentration is on Investable Funds or NAV — this choice cannot be changed mid-tenure.
